feedback.problem: Given the sphere ${x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+(z-1)^{2}=2,$ what is the domain of $z=z(x,y)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the equation of the sphere, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2}+(z-1)^{2} & =2 \\ (z-1)^{2} & =2-({x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2}) \\ z-1 & =\pm \sqrt{2-({x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2})} \\ z & =1\pm \sqrt{2-({x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the square root is defined only for non-negative arguments, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2-({x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2})\ge 0 \\ {x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2}\le 2\end{aligned}
$$

This inequality describes the interior and boundary of the circle 

$$
{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2}=2
$$

which is a circle of radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at $(0,-3)$ in the $xy$-plane.

submitted_fields.submitted_value: The interior and boundary of the circle of radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at $(0,-3)$
